title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第五十 王羲之
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第五十 王羲之 Volume 80 Biographies 50: Wang Xizhi

sentences.zh: 王羲之

translations.literal: Wang Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi

sentences.zh: 王羲之，字逸少，司徒導之從子也。

translations.literal: Wang Xizhi, courtesy name Yishao, was a nephew of Minister of Education Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi, whose courtesy name was Yishao, was a nephew of Wang Dao, the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 祖正，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zheng was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Zheng had served as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父曠，淮南太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuang was Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Kuang was the Administrator of Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, Kuang was the first to initiate the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan prepared to cross south of the Yangzi, Wang Kuang had been the first to advance the plan.

sentences.zh: 羲之幼訥於言，人未之奇。

translations.literal: In youth Xizhi was slow of speech, and people did not regard him as remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Wang Xizhi was tongue-tied, and no one thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he once visited Zhou Yi; Yi observed him and considered him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he paid a call on Zhou Yi, who sized him up and saw something uncommon in him.

sentences.zh: 時重牛心炙，坐客未啖，顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名。

translations.literal: At the time ox-heart roast was prized; the seated guests had not yet eaten when Yi first carved and fed Xizhi, and from this he first became known.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-heart roast was then considered a great delicacy. Before the other guests had tasted it, Zhou Yi carved a portion and offered it to Wang Xizhi, and only then did the boy begin to make a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 及長，辯贍，以骨鯁稱，尤善隸書，為古今之冠，論者稱其筆勢，以為飄若浮雲，矯若驚龍。

translations.literal: When grown, he was eloquent and ample in speech, famed for moral backbone, and especially skilled in clerical script, being the crown of ancient and modern; commentators praised his brush momentum, deeming it drifting like floating clouds, vigorous like startled dragons.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he grew fluent and forceful in debate and was admired for his uncompromising integrity. Above all he excelled at clerical script, standing unrivaled across the ages. Critics described the movement of his brush as drifting like wind-borne clouds and as swift and powerful as a dragon startled into flight.

sentences.zh: 深為從伯敦、導所器重。

translations.literal: He was deeply esteemed by his paternal uncles Dun and Dao.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles Wang Dun and Wang Dao thought the world of him.

sentences.zh: 時陳留阮裕有重名，為敦主簿。

translations.literal: At the time Ruan Yu of Chenliu had a great reputation and was chief clerk to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu of Chenliu enjoyed wide renown at the time and served as chief clerk to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 敦嘗謂羲之曰：「汝是吾家佳子弟，當不減阮主簿。

translations.literal: Dun once said to Xizhi, "You are a fine young man of our house; you ought not fall short of Clerk Ruan."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun once told him, "You are one of the best youths in our clan; you should prove a match for Clerk Ruan."

sentences.zh: 」裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。

translations.literal: Yu also regarded Xizhi with Wang Cheng and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: For his part, Ruan Yu named Wang Xizhi, Wang Cheng, and Wang Yue the three outstanding younger men of the Wang family.

sentences.zh: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導，導令就東廂遍觀子弟。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Xi Jian sent a student to seek a son-in-law from Dao; Dao ordered him to go to the east wing and survey all the young men.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xi Jian dispatched a disciple to ask Wang Dao for a son-in-law, and Wang Dao had the man go to the eastern wing and look over every young kinsman present.

sentences.zh: 門生歸，謂鑒曰：「王氏諸少並佳，然聞信至，咸自矜持。

translations.literal: The student returned and said to Jian, "The young men of the Wang clan are all excellent, yet when they heard the messenger had come, all restrained themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger returned he reported to Xi Jian, "The Wang youths are all impressive, but the moment they learned a matchmaker had arrived, each of them stiffened into his best behavior."

sentences.zh: 惟一人在東床坦腹食，獨若不聞。

translations.literal: Only one man on the eastern couch ate with belly bared, alone as if he had not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Only one sat on the eastern couch with his shirt open, eating unconcernedly as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「正此佳婿邪！

translations.literal: Jian said, "Just this one is the fine son-in-law!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian said, "That is exactly the son-in-law I want."

sentences.zh: 」訪之，乃羲之也，遂以女妻之。

translations.literal: They inquired; it was Xizhi, and so they gave him their daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: They asked who he was: it was Wang Xizhi, and Xi Jian gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，累遷長史。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Palace Secretary; General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang invited him to be an army adviser, and he was promoted repeatedly to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered office as a Gentleman of the Palace Library. Yu Liang, the General Who Conquers the West, recruited him as an army adviser, and he rose step by step to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁。

translations.literal: When Liang was near death, he submitted a memorial praising Xizhi as pure, noble, and possessed of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yu Liang memorialized the throne, commending Wang Xizhi for his integrity, high standing, and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 遷甯遠將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Distance and appointed Inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 羲之既少有美譽，朝廷公卿皆愛其才器，頻召為侍中、吏部尚書，皆不就。

translations.literal: Xizhi, having from youth enjoyed a fine reputation, was loved by the court dukes and ministers for his talent and capacity; he was repeatedly summoned as Palace Attendant and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, but in each case did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi had been celebrated since his early years, and the great officers at court prized his gifts; they called him repeatedly to serve as Palace Attendant and as Minister of Personnel, but he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 復授護軍將軍，又推遷不拜。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Guards the Army, and again deferred and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of General Who Guards the Army and once more put it off without assuming the commission.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史殷浩素雅重之，勸使應命，乃遺羲之書曰：「悠悠者以足下出處足觀政之隆替，如吾等亦謂為然。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Yin Hao had long esteemed him and urged him to answer the summons; he then sent Xizhi a letter saying, "The multitude take your taking office or not as sufficient to observe the rise and decline of government; we too consider it so."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, the Inspector of Yang province, had always held him in high regard and pressed him to accept. Yin wrote to Wang Xizhi: "Gossip holds that whether you serve or withdraw is itself a barometer of good or bad government—and people like me agree."

sentences.zh: 至如足下出處，正與隆替對，豈可以一世之存亡，必從足下從容之適？

translations.literal: As for your taking office or not, it directly faces rise and decline; how can the survival or perishing of an age necessarily follow your leisurely ease?
translations.idiomatic: Your choice to serve or stay out stands directly opposite the fortunes of the state. Surely the rise or fall of an entire era cannot hinge on your personal comfort and convenience."

sentences.zh: 幸徐求眾心。

translations.literal: Hopefully slowly seek the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will move gradually and win the confidence of the people."

sentences.zh: 卿不時起，復可以求美政不？

translations.literal: If you do not rise in due time, can you again seek good government?
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to take up office when the moment calls for it, how can you ever hope to see good government again?"

sentences.zh: 若豁然開懷，當知萬物之情也。

translations.literal: If you open your bosom suddenly, you ought to know the dispositions of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Once you open your mind, you will understand how the world truly feels."

sentences.zh: 」羲之遂報書曰：「吾素自無廊廟志，直王丞相時果欲內吾，誓不許之，手跡猶存，由來尚矣，不於足下參政而方進退。

translations.literal: Xizhi then replied with a letter saying, "I have from of old had no ambition for the court; when Chancellor Wang truly wished to bring me in, I swore not to permit it; the handwriting still exists, it has been long thus; it is not at your entering government that I then advance or retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi answered: "I have never aspired to high ministerial rank. When Chancellor Wang once tried to bring me into the administration, I swore I would not go—the letter he wrote me is still in my keeping, and my resolve has been clear for years. I am not only now, as you take power, deciding whether to step forward or back."

sentences.zh: 自兒娶女嫁，便懷尚子平之志，數與親知言之，非一日也。

translations.literal: From when sons married and daughters wed, I then cherished the ambition of Shang Ziping, and several times spoke of it to kin and friends; it is not one day.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since my sons married and my daughters were given away, I have nursed the wish, like Shang Ziping of old, to leave public life; I have said as much to family and friends again and again, and not just yesterday."

sentences.zh: 若蒙驅使，關隴、巴蜀皆所不辭。

translations.literal: If I receive orders to be dispatched, Guan, Long, Ba, and Shu I all do not decline.
translations.idiomatic: If I am ordered on a mission, I would not refuse even the road to Guanzhong, Longyou, or the Ba–Shu region."

sentences.zh: 吾雖無專對之能，直謹守時命，宣國家威德，固當不同於凡使，必令遠近咸知朝廷留心於無外，此所益殊不同居護軍也。

translations.literal: Although I lack the ability for special diplomatic replies, simply strictly keeping timely orders and proclaiming the state's awe-inspiring virtue, solidly ought to differ from ordinary envoys, necessarily causing far and near all to know the court attends to what is beyond the borders; this benefit is extremely different from occupying Guarding the Army.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack the eloquence of a seasoned negotiator, but if I simply obey the court's commission and make known its majesty and benevolence, I can still do more than the usual envoy: I would show every quarter that the throne cares for the world beyond our borders. That service would be far more useful than warming a seat as General Who Guards the Army."

sentences.zh: 漢末使太傅馬日磾慰撫關東，若不以吾輕微，無所為疑，宜及初冬以行，吾惟恭以待命。」

translations.literal: At the end of Han they sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi to comfort and pacify Guandong; if you do not because I am slight have what to doubt, it is fitting to go by early winter; I only respectfully await orders."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Han the court sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi east of the passes on a mission of consolation. If my low rank does not disqualify me, and you have no misgivings, I should leave in early winter. I await your command with all deference."

sentences.zh: 羲之既拜護軍，又苦求宣城郡，不許，乃以為右軍將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: After Xizhi had accepted Guarding the Army, he also bitterly sought Xuancheng commandery; it was not permitted, and so he was made General of the Right Army and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi did accept the post of General Who Guards the Army, then pleaded repeatedly for Xuancheng commandery. When that was denied, he was appointed General of the Right Army and internal administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 時殷浩與桓溫不協，羲之以國家之安在於內外和，因以與浩書以戒之，浩不從。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Hao and Huan Wen were not harmonious; Xizhi took the state's security as lying in inner and outer harmony, and therefore wrote to Hao to warn him; Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao and Huan Wen were at odds. Wang Xizhi believed the realm could be secure only if court and frontier remained at peace, so he wrote to admonish Yin Hao, who paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 及浩將北伐，羲之以為必敗，以書止之，言甚切至。

translations.literal: When Hao was about to conduct a northern expedition, Xizhi thought it would certainly fail, and with a letter stopped him; the words were very urgent and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao prepared a northern campaign, Wang Xizhi was convinced it would end in disaster and sent him a letter urging him to desist, in the frankest terms.

sentences.zh: 浩遂行果為姚襄所敗。

translations.literal: Hao then proceeded and indeed was defeated by Yao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao went ahead anyway and was routed by Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 復圖再舉，又遺浩書曰：

translations.literal: Again planning a second undertaking, he again sent Hao a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yin plotted a second offensive, Wang Xizhi wrote to him again:

sentences.zh: 知安西敗喪，公私惋怛，不能須臾去懷，以區區江左，所營綜如此，天下寒心，固以久矣，而加之敗喪，此可熟念。

translations.literal: Knowing the General of the West's defeat and loss, public and private are grieved; unable for a moment to leave it from the breast—with the petty Jiangzuo, what is managed and brought together is thus; the realm's hearts are cold, solidly it has been long, and adding defeat and loss, this can be pondered maturely.
translations.idiomatic: The news of the defeat of the army under the General of the West has left everyone, official and commoner alike, heartsick; the sorrow will not lift. Our modest foothold south of the Yangzi has been governed to this pass; the empire has long been disheartened, and now this rout on top of everything—think hard about what that means.

sentences.zh: 往事豈復可追，顧思弘將來，令天下寄命有所，自隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Past affairs how again can be pursued; look to thinking broadly the future, causing the realm to entrust life to have a place, from this raising the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be undone. Look instead to the future: give the people something solid to live for, and you will yourself enlarge the work of restoring the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 政以道勝寬和為本，力爭武功，作非所當，因循所長，以固大業，想識其由來也。

translations.literal: Government takes the Way's victory and lenient harmony as root; striving forcefully for military merit, acting not what is appropriate, following what is long in one, to solidify the great enterprise—I suppose you recognize whence it comes.
translations.idiomatic: Good rule rests on moral ascendancy and a calm, generous temper; to strain after military glory when the time is wrong is a mistake. Play to your strengths and shore up the great enterprise—you know this as well as I.

sentences.zh: 自寇亂以來，處內外之任者，未有深謀遠慮，括囊至計，而疲竭根本，各從所志，竟無一功可論，一事可記，忠言嘉謀棄而莫用，遂令天下將有土崩之勢，何能不痛心悲慨也。

translations.literal: Since the bandit turmoil, those occupying inner and outer responsibilities have not had deep plans and far considerations, tying the bag's utmost schemes, but exhausted the root, each following their ambitions; in the end not one merit can be discussed, not one affair can be recorded; loyal words and fine plans are discarded and not used, thus causing the realm about to have the momentum of landslide—how can one not be pained in heart and grieved!
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellions began, those who have held office at court and on the borders have shown neither foresight nor a coherent strategy. They have drained the state's foundations while each pursued private aims, and not a single success or memorable deed has come of it. Sound counsel is thrown aside, and the empire now teeters toward collapse—how can we not feel bitter grief?

sentences.zh: 任其事者，豈得辭四海之責！

translations.literal: Those entrusted with these affairs, how can they decline responsibility for the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: Those who bear this burden cannot escape accountability to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 追咎往事，亦何所復及，宜更虛己求賢，當與有識共之，不可復令忠允之言常屈於當權。

translations.literal: Pursuing blame for past affairs, again what is there to reach; it is fitting further to empty self and seek the worthy, ought to share with those who have insight; it cannot again cause loyal and candid words constantly to be bent under those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Recriminations over the past accomplish nothing. Humble yourself, seek out able men, and work with those who see clearly; do not let honest advice be silenced again by whoever happens to hold power.

sentences.zh: 今軍破於外，資竭於內，保淮之志非復所及，莫過還保長江，都督將各復舊鎮，自長江以外，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Now the army is broken outside, resources exhausted inside; the ambition to hold the Huai is no longer reachable; nothing surpasses returning to guard the Yangzi; supervising generals each restore old garrisons; from beyond the Yangzi, loose rein only.
translations.idiomatic: The field armies are shattered and the treasury is empty; we can no longer dream of holding the Huai line. The best we can do is fall back to the Yangzi, send each commander to his old post, and treat everything beyond the river as ground we merely influence at a distance.

sentences.zh: 任國鈞者，引咎責躬，深自貶降以謝百姓。

translations.literal: Those who bear the state's weight should draw blame and blame the self, deeply self-demote to apologize to the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers must own their faults, humble themselves, and make amends to the people.

sentences.zh: 更與朝賢思布平政，除其煩苛，省其賦役，與百姓更始。

translations.literal: Further with court worthies think to spread level government, remove their vexatious harshness, reduce their levies and corvée, with the hundred surnames make a new beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Then join the worthy men at court in planning honest administration: strip away oppressive regulations, lighten taxes and labor service, and give the common people a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 庶可以允塞群望，救倒懸之急。

translations.literal: Perhaps thereby can satisfy and block the multitude's hopes, rescue the urgency of inverted hanging.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus can you answer what the country expects of you and ease the desperate straits we are in.

sentences.zh: 使君起于布衣，任天下之重，尚德之舉，未能事事允稱。

translations.literal: The envoy lord rose from plain cloth, bearing the heaviness of the realm; the promotion of virtue's undertaking has not been able in every affair to be fittingly praised.
translations.idiomatic: You began as a commoner and now shoulder the fate of the empire; even the best intentions cannot make every deed meet everyone's praise.

sentences.zh: 當董統之任而敗喪至此，恐闔朝群賢未有與人分其謗者。

translations.literal: When bearing the duty of supervising and unifying yet defeat and loss reach here, I fear the whole court's group of worthies has none who share with others their slander.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with supreme command, you have brought us to this disaster; I doubt anyone else at court will step forward to share the blame with you.

sentences.zh: 今亟修德補闕，廣延群賢，與之分任，尚未知獲濟所期。

translations.literal: Now urgently cultivate virtue and mend gaps, broadly extend the group of worthies, with them divide responsibilities, still not knowing to obtain relief of what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Repair your moral standing at once, widen your circle of able advisers, and share power with them—only then might we see whether the situation can be saved.

sentences.zh: 若猶以前事為未工，故復求之於分外，宇宙雖廣，自容何所！

translations.literal: If still taking former affairs as not skillful, therefore again seeking them beyond one's portion, though the cosmos is wide, where is self-accommodation!
translations.idiomatic: If you still think you have not failed and reach for still more beyond your proper role, the world is vast—yet where will you find room for yourself?

sentences.zh: 知言不必用，或取怨執政，然當情慨所在，正自不能不盡懷極言。

translations.literal: Knowing words need not be used, perhaps incurring resentment of those in power, yet where feeling and indignation lie, just from self cannot but fully in the breast speak to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I know blunt advice may not be heeded and may anger those who govern, but the heart's outrage leaves me no choice but to speak my mind completely.

sentences.zh: 若必親征，未達此旨，果行者，愚智所不解也。

translations.literal: If you must personally campaign, not comprehending this purport, if indeed proceeding, fool and wise do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on taking the field in person without grasping this point, and actually go through with it, neither the dull nor the clever will understand your reasoning.

sentences.zh: 願復與眾共之。

translations.literal: I wish again to share with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to deliberate again with the assembly.

sentences.zh: 復被州符，增運千石，征役兼至，皆以軍期，對之喪氣，罔知所厝。

translations.literal: Again receiving provincial writs, increasing transport a thousand shi, conscript labor arriving together, all with military deadlines; facing it loses breath, not knowing where to place.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh orders from the province demand another thousand shi of grain and simultaneous levies of labor, all on military deadlines. The people are demoralized and do not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 自頃年割剝遺黎，刑徒竟路，殆同秦政，惟未加參夷之刑耳，恐勝廣之憂，無復日矣。

translations.literal: Since recent years carving and stripping the surviving black-haired ones, punished convicts filling the road, roughly equal to Qin government, only not yet adding the three-clans extermination punishment; I fear Chen Sheng and Wu Guang's worry, no again day.
translations.idiomatic: For years the remnant population has been bled white; shackled convicts choke the highways—policy almost as harsh as the Qin, short only of mass executions by kinship. I fear a Chen Sheng–style uprising may not be far off.

sentences.zh: 又與會稽王箋陳浩不宜北伐，並論時事曰：

translations.literal: He also sent a note to the Prince of Kuaiji stating Hao should not northern expedition, and discussing the times' affairs saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to the Prince of Kuaiji arguing that Yin Hao must not launch another northern campaign, and commented on the state of the realm:

sentences.zh: 古人恥其君不為堯舜，北面之道，豈不願尊其所事，比靈斯往代，況遇千載一時之運？

translations.literal: The ancients were ashamed if their lord was not Yao and Shun; the way of facing north, how not wish to honor what they serve, compare spirit with former ages, moreover encountering a thousand years one time's fortune?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients were ashamed to serve any ruler who fell short of Yao and Shun. As subjects we all wish to exalt our sovereign and rank him with the sage-kings of old—especially when fate offers a once-in-a-millennium chance.

sentences.zh: 顧智力屈于當年，何得不權輕重而處之也。

translations.literal: But intelligence and strength are bent in the present year; how can one not weigh light and heavy and dispose of it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet talent and strength are limited in our own day; we have no choice but to weigh priorities carefully and act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今雖有可欣之會，內求諸己，而所憂乃重於所欣。

translations.literal: Now although there is a meeting that can be rejoiced in, inwardly seeking in oneself, yet what is worried about is heavier than what is rejoiced in.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly there may be cause for hope, but when I look within, what troubles me outweighs what encourages me.

sentences.zh: 《傳》云：「自非聖人，外甯必有內憂。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "If not oneself a sage, outer peace necessarily has inner worry."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says, "Unless one is a sage, outward calm always brings inner trouble."

sentences.zh: 」今外不寧，內憂已深。

translations.literal: Now outer is not tranquil; inner worry is already deep.
translations.idiomatic: Our borders are not secure, and domestic troubles run deep.

sentences.zh: 古之弘大業者，或不謀於眾，傾國以濟一時功者，亦往往而有之。

translations.literal: Those of old who enlarged great enterprises sometimes did not plan with the multitude; those who overturned the state to accomplish a moment's merit also often existed.
translations.idiomatic: Great founders of old sometimes acted without consulting everyone, and rulers who staked the whole kingdom on a single gamble are hardly unknown.

sentences.zh: 誠獨運之明足以邁眾，暫勞之弊終獲永逸者可也。

translations.literal: Truly if solitary operation's clarity suffices to surpass the multitude, temporary toil's harm finally obtains lasting ease, it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: That can work only when one man's vision truly outshines all others and a spell of hardship buys lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 求之於今，可得擬議乎！

translations.literal: Seeking it in the present, can one compare and discuss!
translations.idiomatic: Can you honestly say our present circumstances fit that pattern?

sentences.zh: 夫廟算決勝，必宜審量彼我，萬全而後動。

translations.literal: Now temple calculation deciding victory, necessarily should carefully measure them and us, ten thousand completeness and then move.
translations.idiomatic: Victory decided in council demands a sober reckoning of enemy and self: move only when every advantage is secured.

sentences.zh: 功就之日，便當因其眾而即其實。

translations.literal: The day merit is accomplished, then ought according to their multitude to approach their reality.
translations.idiomatic: When success is won, you must match your forces to the real situation on the ground.

sentences.zh: 今功未可期，而遺黎殲盡，萬不餘一。

translations.literal: Now merit is not yet expectable, yet the surviving black-haired ones are exterminated utterly, of ten thousand not one remains.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot count on victory, yet the people who survived the last disasters have been wiped out—hardly one in ten thousand remains.

sentences.zh: 且千里饋糧，自古為難，況今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河。

translations.literal: Moreover a thousand li feeding grain, from antiquity is difficult, moreover now transport supplying continuation, west conveying to Xu-Luo, north entering the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Supplying an army over a thousand li has always been difficult; today convoys must run west toward Xuchang and Luoyang and north to the Yellow River as well.

sentences.zh: 雖秦政之弊，未至於此，而十室之憂，便以交至。

translations.literal: Although Qin government's harms did not reach here, yet ten houses' worries then with cross arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Even the harshness of the Qin never pushed every village to this edge of despair, yet household after household now faces ruin at once.

sentences.zh: 今運無還期，徵求日重，以區區吳越經緯天下十分之九，不亡何待！

translations.literal: Now transport has no return period, exactions daily heavy, with the petty Wu-Yue weaving the realm's nine tenths, not perishing what waits!
translations.idiomatic: There is no end in sight to the convoys, and levies grow heavier by the day. Our small Wu–Yue region is asked to carry nine-tenths of the empire—if we are not destroyed, what are we waiting for?

sentences.zh: 而不度德量力，不弊不已，此封內所痛心歎悼而莫敢吐誠。

translations.literal: Yet not measuring virtue and weighing strength, not exhausted not stop—this within the domain is what pains the heart and sighs in grief yet none dares spit sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Still you refuse to measure your moral authority or material strength, and you will not stop until everything is broken—this is what every subject grieves in silence, too afraid to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 往者不可諫，來者猶可追，願殿下更垂三思，解而更張，令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵，許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城諸軍皆還保淮，為不可勝之基，鬚根立勢舉，謀之未晚，此實當今策之上者。

translations.literal: The gone cannot be remonstrated; the coming still can be pursued; I wish the Prince again drop three thoughts, untie and restring, causing Yin Hao, Xun Xian to return and occupy Hefei, Guangling, Xuchang, Qiao commandery, Liang, Pengcheng various armies all return to guard the Huai, as foundation of invincibility; when beard root stands momentum rises, planning it is not late—this truly is of present strategies the highest.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be undone, but the future can still be mended. I beg Your Highness to think three times more, change course, and pull Yin Hao and Xun Xian back to hold Hefei and Guangling while the troops at Xuchang, Qiao, Liang, and Pengcheng all withdraw to the Huai line. That would lay a foundation no enemy could easily overthrow; once our roots are firm and our posture secure, you may plan further—it will not be too late. This is the best policy open to us today.

sentences.zh: 若不行此，社稷之憂可計日而待。

translations.literal: If this is not done, the altars of soil and grain's worry can be counted by days and awaited.
translations.idiomatic: If you reject this course, the fall of the dynasty can be reckoned in days.

sentences.zh: 安危之機，易於反掌，考之虛實，著於目前，願運獨斷之明，定之於一朝也。

translations.literal: The pivot of safety and danger is easier than turning the palm; examining its emptiness and fullness, manifest before the eyes; I wish you exercise solitary decisiveness's clarity, settle it in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: The turn between survival and ruin is as quick as flipping a hand; the facts are plain before your eyes. I pray you use your own decisive judgment and settle the matter in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 地淺而言深，豈不知其未易。

translations.literal: Position shallow yet words deep, how not know it is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: My rank is low and my words weighty—I know how unwelcome that can be.

sentences.zh: 然古人處閭閻行陣之間，尚或幹時謀國，評裁者不以為譏，況廁大臣末行，豈可默而不言哉！

translations.literal: Yet the ancients between lanes and alleys and battle lines, still sometimes managed the times and planned the state; evaluators did not consider it blame, moreover ranking in great ministers' lowest row, how can be silent and not speak!
translations.idiomatic: Yet men of old, though they stood only among common soldiers or in the marketplace, sometimes shaped the age and served the state, and thoughtful critics did not mock them. How much less may I, who sit even among the great officers, hold my tongue?

sentences.zh: 存亡所系，決在行之，不可復持疑後機，不定之於此，後欲悔之，亦無及也。

translations.literal: Survival and perishing what hangs on, decided in practicing it; cannot again hold doubt delaying opportunity; not deciding here, afterward wishing to regret it, also there is no reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Our survival hangs on action now. Hesitate past the moment, fail to decide here, and remorse will come too late.

sentences.zh: 殿下德冠宇內，以公室輔朝，最可直道行之，致隆當年，而未允物望，受殊遇者所以寤寐長歎，實為殿下惜之。

translations.literal: Your Highness's virtue crowns within the cosmos, with the ducal house assisting the court, most can straight Way practice it, causing loftiness in the present year, yet not satisfying things' hopes; those receiving special favor therefore sleeping and waking long sigh, truly for Your Highness regrets it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's virtue is unmatched, and as prince of the blood you aid the throne—no one is better placed to follow the straight path and bring this era to greatness. Yet you have not matched what the world expects, and those of us who enjoy your special favor lie awake sighing, sorry on your account.

sentences.zh: 國家之慮深矣，常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔，麋鹿之游將不止林藪而已。

translations.literal: The state's worry is deep; constantly fear Wu Yuan's worry is not only in the past; elk's roaming will not stop at forests and marshes only.
translations.idiomatic: The dangers before the state are grave. I fear Wu Zixu's warning is not confined to antiquity, and that deer will graze in our palace yards, not only in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 願殿下暫廢虛遠之懷，以救倒懸之急，可謂以亡為存，轉禍為福，則宗廟之慶，四海有賴矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Highness temporarily abandon empty far thoughts, to rescue inverted hanging's urgency; can be called taking perishing as survival, turning misfortune as blessing; then the ancestral temples' celebration, the four seas have reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside lofty abstractions for a time and address the crisis that hangs us head down: that is how to snatch survival from ruin and turn peril into blessing. The imperial house would rejoice, and the realm would have something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 時東土饑荒，羲之輒開倉振貸。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern lands had famine; Xizhi then opened granaries and relieved with loans.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the eastern regions, and Wang Xizhi opened the government granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷賦役繁重，吳會憂甚，羲之每上疏爭之，事多見從。

translations.literal: Yet the court's levies and corvée were heavy and numerous; Wu and Hui were greatly worried; Xizhi often submitted memorials disputing them; affairs were mostly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's taxes and labor demands remained crushing, and the Wu–Kuaiji area suffered acutely. Wang Xizhi repeatedly memorialized against the policy, and the throne often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie An a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Xie An, the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing:

sentences.zh: 頃所陳論，每蒙允納，所以令下小得蘇息，各安其業。

translations.literal: Recently what was stated in discussion, each time received permission and acceptance; therefore causing orders below slightly to obtain recovery and rest, each secure in their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The points I have raised have usually won your approval, so that local directives give the people a little breathing room and let them stay at their work in peace.

sentences.zh: 若不耳，此一郡久以蹈東海矣。

translations.literal: If not so, this one commandery long since would have stepped into the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Without that, this commandery would long ago have followed Lu Zhonglian into the eastern sea—meaning revolt or mass flight.

sentences.zh: 今事之大者未布，漕運是也。

translations.literal: Now of affairs the great ones not yet spread, grain transport is this.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest problem still unsettled is the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 吾意望朝廷可申下定期，委之所司，勿復催下，但當歲終考其殿最。

translations.literal: My meaning hopes the court can extend below fixed periods, entrust to those in charge, do not again urge below, only ought at year's end examine their best and worst.
translations.idiomatic: I hope the court will set clear deadlines, leave execution to the responsible offices, stop sending down endless urgings, and judge officials only at year's end by their performance ratings.

sentences.zh: 長吏尤殿，命檻車送詣天臺。

translations.literal: Senior officials especially worst, order caged cart send to celestial terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Any magistrate who ranks worst should be sent to the capital in a prison cart.

sentences.zh: 三縣不舉，二千石必免，或可左降，令在疆塞極難之地。

translations.literal: Three counties not raising, two thousand shi necessarily dismissed, or perhaps demoted left, ordered to be at border passes extremely difficult places.
translations.idiomatic: If three districts fail their quotas, the local two-thousand-shi official must be removed—perhaps demoted and posted to some perilous frontier.

sentences.zh: 又自吾到此，從事常有四五，兼以台司及都水御史行台文符如雨，倒錯違背，不復可知。

translations.literal: Moreover since I arrived here, attendants often have four or five, combined with terrace office and capital water censor mobile terrace documents like rain, inverted wrong contrary violate, no longer knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took this post I have had four or five assistants at a time, while edicts from the central ministries, the capital hydraulics office, and the touring censorates rain down—contradictory, confused, impossible to sort out.

sentences.zh: 吾又瞑目循常推前，取重者及綱紀，輕者在五曹。

translations.literal: I also close eyes follow routine push forward; taking heavy ones reach clerks and scribes, light ones are in five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: I shut my eyes, follow routine, and push papers along: weighty items go to the senior clerks, lighter ones to the five bureaus.

sentences.zh: 主者蒞事，未嘗得十日，吏民趨走，功費萬計。

translations.literal: Those in charge attending affairs, never obtain ten days; clerks and people rush about, merit expense in myriads counted.
translations.idiomatic: No officer ever gets ten uninterrupted days on a task; clerks and commoners run themselves ragged, and the waste runs into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 卿方任其重，可徐尋所言。

translations.literal: You just bear its heaviness; can slowly seek what was said.
translations.idiomatic: You now shoulder heavy responsibility; please give these suggestions your careful attention.

sentences.zh: 江左平日，揚州一良刺史便足統之，況以群才而更不理，正由為法不一，牽制者眾，思簡而易從，便足以保守成業

translations.literal: Jiangzuo ordinary days, Yang Province one good Inspector then suffices to unify it, moreover with group talent yet more not governed, exactly because as law not one, those who restrain are many; thinking simple and easy to follow, then suffices to protect and guard accomplished enterprise
translations.idiomatic: In normal times south of the Yangzi a single capable Inspector of Yang province was enough to keep order; with so many talented men under you, disorder persists only because regulations conflict and too many hands pull in different directions. Simplify the rules so they are easy to obey, and you can preserve what we have

sentences.zh: 倉督監耗盜官米，動以萬計，吾謂誅翦一人，其後便斷，而時意不同。

translations.literal: Granary supervisors waste and steal official rice, moving by myriads counted; I said execute and cut one person, afterward then stops, yet the time's intent differed.
translations.idiomatic: Granary overseers embezzle tens of thousands of bushels of state grain. I argued that executing one ringleader would stop the rest, but opinion at court disagreed.

sentences.zh: 近檢校諸縣，無不皆爾。

translations.literal: Recently inspecting various counties, none not all thus.
translations.idiomatic: A recent audit of the counties shows the same abuse everywhere.

sentences.zh: 余姚近十萬斛，重斂以資奸吏，令國用空乏，良可歎也。

translations.literal: Yuyao nearly one hundred thousand hu, heavy levies to supply wicked clerks, causing state use empty and lacking, truly can be sighed over.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyao alone is short nearly a hundred thousand hu because harsh exactions feed corrupt underlings and leave the treasury bare—a sorry state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 自軍興以來，征役及充運死亡叛散不反者眾，虛耗至此，而補代循常，所在凋困，莫知所出。

translations.literal: Since military rising, conscript labor and filling transport death, defection, scattering, not returning are many; empty waste reaches here, yet replacement follows routine; everywhere withered and distressed, none knows what emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, huge numbers have died, deserted, or vanished on corvée and transport duty. The population is hollowed out, yet replacements are drafted on the old pattern; every district is exhausted and no one sees a way out.

sentences.zh: 上命所差，上道多叛，則吏及叛者席捲同去。

translations.literal: Those whom superior orders dispatch, on the road many rebel, then clerks and rebels roll up mat and go together.
translations.idiomatic: Men drafted by imperial order often desert the moment they set out; local clerks then flee together with the runaways, and whole districts are stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 又有常制，輒令其家及同伍課捕。

translations.literal: Moreover there is standing regulation, always ordering their families and same-five-unit to impose capture.
translations.idiomatic: Standing rules then hold the man's family and his five-household mutual-responsibility group liable for hunting him down.

sentences.zh: 課捕不擒，家及同伍尋復亡叛。

translations.literal: If imposed capture does not seize, family and same-five-unit soon again flee and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When those roundups fail, the same families and neighbors soon desert in turn.

sentences.zh: 百姓流亡，戶口日減，其源在此。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames drift in exile, household registers daily decrease; the source is here.
translations.idiomatic: The people scatter and the population registers shrink day by day—this is where the rot begins.

sentences.zh: 又有百工醫寺，死亡絕沒，家戶空盡，差代無所，上命不絕，事起成十年、十五年，彈舉獲罪無懈息而無益實事，何以堪之！

translations.literal: Moreover there are hundred craftsmen and medical temples; death cuts off extinction, households empty utterly, replacement dispatch has nowhere, superior orders unceasing, affairs arising become ten years, fifteen years, impeachment and offense without slack rest yet no benefit to real affairs—how can one bear it!
translations.idiomatic: The same plague hits artisans and monastic infirmaries: workers die out, families vanish, and there is no one left to fill the quotas—yet edicts keep coming. Cases drag on ten or fifteen years; denunciations and punishments never pause while nothing useful gets done. How long can we endure this?

sentences.zh: 謂自今諸死罪原輕者及五歲刑，可以充此，其減死者，可長充兵役，五歲者，可充雜工醫寺，皆令移其家以實都邑。

translations.literal: I say from now all death crimes originally light and five-year punishments can fill this; those whose death is reduced can long fill military service; five-year ones can fill miscellaneous labor and medical temples; all order moving their households to fill capital cities.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, commute lighter capital cases and five-year sentences into these slots: spare the condemned from execution and assign them instead to lifelong military labor; assign five-year convicts to workshops and temple clinics—and move their entire households into the capital to thicken the population.

sentences.zh: 都邑既實，是政之本，又可絕其亡叛。

translations.literal: Capital cities once filled, this is government's root; also can cut off their fleeing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A full capital is the foundation of sound rule, and it keeps those workers from running away.

sentences.zh: 不移其家，逃亡之患復如初耳。

translations.literal: If not moving their households, the harm of flight returns as at first.
translations.idiomatic: If their families are not relocated, we are right back to the old desertion problem.

sentences.zh: 今除罪而充雜役，盡移其家，小人愚迷，或以為重於殺戮，可以絕奸。

translations.literal: Now removing crime and filling miscellaneous labor, entirely moving their households, petty men foolish and deluded, perhaps think it heavier than slaughter, can cut off wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing execution with penal service and resettling whole clans may strike common folk as harsher than killing, yet it can choke off corruption.

sentences.zh: 刑名雖輕，懲肅實重，豈非適時之宜邪！

translations.literal: Though punishment's name is light, warning and awe are truly heavy—is this not timely fitness!
translations.idiomatic: The statute looks mild, but the deterrent is severe—precisely what the times require.

sentences.zh: 羲之雅好服食養性，不樂在京師，初渡浙江，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Xizhi elegantly loved ingesting medicines and nurturing nature, not happy in the capital; when first crossing the Zhe River, then had the will to end there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi cultivated his temperament with elixirs and regimen and disliked life at court; the first time he crossed the Zhe River he resolved to end his days in the south.

sentences.zh: 會稽有佳山水，名士多居之，謝安未仕時亦居焉。

translations.literal: Kuaiji has fine mountains and waters; famous scholars mostly dwell there; Xie An when not yet in office also dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji boasted superb landscape, and celebrated gentlemen clustered there; Xie An had lived there too before he took office.

sentences.zh: 孫綽、李充、許詢、支遁等皆以文義冠世，並築室東土，與羲之同好。

translations.literal: Sun Chuo, Li Chong, Xu Xun, Zhi Dun and others all with literary meaning crowned the age, together built houses in eastern lands, sharing Xizhi's likes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo, Li Chong, Xu Xun, Zhi Dun, and their circle led the age in letters and learning; they all built homes in the eastern region and shared Wang Xizhi's tastes.

sentences.zh: 嘗與同志宴集于會稽山陰之蘭亭，羲之自為之序以申其志，曰：

translations.literal: Once with like-minded feasted and gathered at Kuaiji Shanyin's Orchid Pavilion; Xizhi himself for it made a preface to declare his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once joined kindred spirits for a banquet at the Orchid Pavilion south of Kuaiji and composed a preface to set out his feelings. It reads:

sentences.zh: 永和九年，歲在癸丑，暮春之初，會於會稽山陰之蘭亭，修禊事也。

translations.literal: Yonghe ninth year, year in guichou, late spring's beginning, met at Kuaiji Shanyin's Orchid Pavilion, was purification-xi affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yonghe, the cyclical year guichou, at the start of late spring, we met at the Orchid Pavilion in Shanyin, Kuaiji, for the spring purification rite.

sentences.zh: 群賢畢至，少長咸集。

translations.literal: Group worthies all arrived; young and old all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Every eminent guest came, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 此地有崇山峻嶺，茂林修竹，又有清流激湍，映帶左右，引以為流觴曲水，列坐其次。

translations.literal: This place has lofty mountains steep ridges, lush forests tall bamboo, also clear streams rushing rapids, reflected girdle left and right, led to make flowing-cup winding water, arrayed seated at its side.
translations.idiomatic: Here rise steep peaks and thick groves of bamboo; clear torrents whirl past on either hand. We channeled them into a winding stream for the floating-cup game and sat in order along its banks.

sentences.zh: 雖無絲竹管弦之盛，一觴一詠，亦足以暢敘幽情。

translations.literal: Although lacking strings and bamboo pipes' splendor, one cup one chant, also suffices to freely express hidden feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Though we had no full orchestra, each cup of wine and each impromptu poem was enough to give voice to our deepest moods.

sentences.zh: 是日也，天朗氣清，惠風和暢，仰觀宇宙之大，俯察品類之盛，所以遊目騁懷，足以極視聽之娛，信可樂也。

translations.literal: This day, sky bright air clear, kind wind mild and smooth, looking up observe cosmos's greatness, looking down inspect myriad kinds' splendor, whereby roaming eyes and racing breast, suffices to exhaust sight and hearing's joy, truly can be joyful.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky shone clear and a gentle breeze blew warm. Looking up, we saw the immensity of the heavens; looking down, the richness of every living thing. The eye wandered freely and the heart opened wide—sight and sound brought pure delight. It was happiness indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫人之相與，俯仰一世，或取諸懷抱，悟言一室之內，或因寄所托，放浪形骸之外。

translations.literal: Now people's mutual dealings, bowing and raising one generation, some take from bosom embrace, awakened words within one room, some by entrusting what relied on, unrestrained beyond form and bones.
translations.idiomatic: Men live out their lives in the turn of a head—some share confidences indoors, others give themselves to wandering beyond all bodily restraint, each according to his bent.

sentences.zh: 雖趣舍萬殊，靜躁不同，當其欣於所遇，暫得於己，快然自足，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: Although inclinations and renunciations ten thousand different, quiet and restless not same, when they rejoice in what they meet, temporarily obtain in self, pleased and self-sufficient, not knowing old age's about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Tastes differ—some restless, some still—but whenever a man meets what delights him and feels at one with the moment, he is content and forgets that age is closing in.

sentences.zh: 及其所之既倦，情隨事遷，感慨系之矣。

translations.literal: When what they went to is already weary, feeling follows affairs shifting, sighs and regrets attach to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the old fascination fades and circumstances change, regret and longing inevitably follow.

sentences.zh: 向之所欣，俯仰之間，已為陳跡，猶不能不以之興懷。

translations.literal: Former what was rejoiced in, between bowing and raising, already becomes old traces, still cannot but by it rouse the breast.
translations.idiomatic: The joys we cherished moments ago are already behind us, yet we cannot keep our hearts from stirring at the thought.

sentences.zh: 況修短隨化，終期於盡。

translations.literal: Moreover long and short follow transformation, end fixed at exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: And whether life lasts long or short, it runs its course to the same end.

sentences.zh: 古人云，死生亦大矣，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: The ancients said, death and life also are great—how not painful!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that death and life are the greatest of matters. Is that not cause for grief?

sentences.zh: 每覽昔人興感之由，若合一契，未嘗不臨文嗟悼，不能喻之於懷。

translations.literal: Each time viewing ancients' rise-sighing's causes, as if joining one tally, never not facing text sighing in grief, unable to explain it in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read old writers on what moves them, it is as if we shared the same stamp; I always pause over their words in sorrow, yet the feeling is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 固知一死生為虛誕，齊彭殤為妄作，後之視今，亦猶今之視昔，悲夫！

translations.literal: Solidly knowing equating death and life is empty absurdity, equalizing Peng and shang is reckless making; later's viewing now, also like now's viewing past—alas!
translations.idiomatic: I know well that to treat life and death as the same is a lie, and to equate the long-lived Peng Zu with a child dead young is sophistry. Future readers will look on our age as we look on the past—how bitter that thought is.

sentences.zh: 故列敘時人，錄其所述，雖世殊事異，所以興懷，其致一也。

translations.literal: Therefore array narrate contemporaries, record what they stated; although ages differ affairs differ, whereby rouse the breast, their aim is one.
translations.idiomatic: So I list the men of today and preserve their poems: later ages will face other times and other cares, yet what moves the heart comes to the same thing.

sentences.zh: 後之覽者，亦將有感於斯文。

translations.literal: Later viewers, also will have feeling toward this text.
translations.idiomatic: Readers who come after us may yet find something of themselves in these lines.

sentences.zh: 或以潘岳《金穀詩序》方其文，羲之比于石崇，聞而甚喜。

translations.literal: Some with Pan Yue's "Jingu Poems Preface" compared his text; Xizhi compared to Shi Chong, hearing was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Some likened his piece to Pan Yue's preface to the Golden Valley poems and compared Wang Xizhi himself to Shi Chong; he was delighted to hear it.

sentences.zh: 性愛鵝，會稽有孤居姥養一鵝，善鳴，求市未能得，遂攜親友命駕就觀。

translations.literal: By nature loved geese; Kuaiji had an old woman living alone raising one goose, good at crying; seeking to buy could not obtain; then carrying kin and friends ordered carriage to go view.
translations.idiomatic: He adored geese. An old widow in Kuaiji kept one with a fine voice; he tried to buy it without success, so he brought friends and rode out to see it.

sentences.zh: 姥聞羲之將至，烹以待之，羲之嘆惜彌日。

translations.literal: The old woman heard Xizhi would arrive, cooked to await him; Xizhi sighed in regret filling the day.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard he was coming she cooked the goose to entertain him; he mourned the loss the whole day through.

sentences.zh: 又山陰有一道士，養好鵝，羲之往觀焉，意甚悅，固求市之。

translations.literal: Also Shanyin had a Daoist priest, raising fine geese; Xizhi went to view them, intent very pleased, firmly sought to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist in Shanyin kept handsome geese. Wang Xizhi went to admire them, was charmed, and pressed to buy the flock.

sentences.zh: 道士云：「為寫《道德經》，當舉群相贈耳。

translations.literal: The Daoist said, "If you copy the Dao De Jing for me, I will give you the whole flock."
translations.idiomatic: The priest said, "Copy the Dao De Jing for me, and the whole flock is yours."

sentences.zh: 」羲之欣然寫畢，籠鵝而歸，甚以為樂。

translations.literal: Xizhi gladly wrote finished, caged geese and returned, greatly took it as joy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi happily finished the copy, caged the birds, and went home in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 其任率如此。

translations.literal: His acting on impulse was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his spontaneous, unstudied manner.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣門生家，見棐幾滑淨，因書之，真草相半。

translations.literal: Once visited a student's home, saw a lacquer table smooth clean, therefore wrote on it, regular and cursive half each.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a disciple's house he saw a polished lacquer table and wrote across it in half regular, half cursive script.

sentences.zh: 後為其父誤刮去之，門生驚懊者累日。

translations.literal: Later by his father mistakenly scraped it away; the student startled and regretful many days.
translations.idiomatic: The boy's father later scraped it off by mistake, and the disciple was beside himself with remorse for days.

sentences.zh: 又嘗在蕺山見一老姥，持六角竹扇賣之。

translations.literal: Also once at Ji Mountain saw an old woman, holding hexagonal bamboo fans selling them.
translations.idiomatic: Another time, on Mount Ji, he met an old woman selling hexagonal bamboo fans.

sentences.zh: 羲之書其扇，各為五字。

translations.literal: Xizhi wrote her fans, each as five characters.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed five characters on each fan.

sentences.zh: 姥初有慍色。

translations.literal: The old woman at first had an angry look.
translations.idiomatic: At first she looked annoyed.

sentences.zh: 因謂姥曰：「但言是王右軍書，以求百錢邪。

translations.literal: Therefore said to the old woman, "Only say it is General of the Right Army's writing, to seek hundred cash."
translations.idiomatic: He told her, "Just say they were written by the General of the Right Army, and you can ask a hundred cash apiece."

sentences.zh: 」姥如其言，人競買之。

translations.literal: The old woman as he said; people competed to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: She did as he said, and buyers snatched them up.

sentences.zh: 他日，姥又持扇來，羲之笑而不答。

translations.literal: Another day, the old woman again brought fans; Xizhi smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When she came back another day with more fans, he only smiled and declined.

sentences.zh: 其書為世所重，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His calligraphy by the age was prized; all was this kind.
translations.idiomatic: The world treasured his brush for reasons like these.

sentences.zh: 每自稱「我書比鐘繇，當抗行；

translations.literal: Often self-called, "My writing compared to Zhong Yao, ought to walk abreast;"
translations.idiomatic: He used to say, "Set my calligraphy beside Zhong Yao's and I can hold my own;

sentences.zh: 比張芝草，猶當雁行也」。

translations.literal: compared to Zhang Zhi's cursive, still ought to be wild-goose line."
translations.idiomatic: set it beside Zhang Zhi's cursive, and I may still walk in the same rank."

sentences.zh: 曾與人書云：「張芝臨池學書，池水盡黑，使人耽之若是，未必後之也。

translations.literal: Once wrote to someone saying, "Zhang Zhi by the pond studied writing, pond water all black; if one made others addicted thus, not necessarily behind him."
translations.idiomatic: In a letter he wrote: "Zhang Zhi practiced so hard by the pond that the water turned black. Devote yourself like that and you need not rank behind him."

sentences.zh: 」羲之書初不勝庾翼、郗愔，及其暮年方妙。

translations.literal: Xizhi's writing at first did not surpass Yu Yi, Xi Yin; reaching his late years then wonderful.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wang Xizhi's hand did not outshine Yu Yi or Xi Yin; only in old age did it become sublime.

sentences.zh: 嘗以章草答庾亮，而翼深歎伏，因與羲之書云：「吾昔有伯英章草十紙，過江顛狽，遂乃亡失，常歎妙跡永絕。

translations.literal: Once with bureauscript cursive answered Yu Liang, and Yi deeply sighed in submission, therefore wrote Xizhi saying, "I formerly had Bo Ying bureauscript cursive ten sheets, crossing river in dire straits, then lost them, constantly sighed wonderful traces forever cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He once replied to Yu Liang in draft cursive; Yu Yi was awestruck and wrote to him: "I once owned ten sheets of Zhang Zhi's draft cursive, but lost them in the chaos of crossing the Yangzi. I thought such masterpieces were gone forever.

sentences.zh: 忽見足下答家兄書，煥若神明，頓還舊觀。」

translations.literal: Suddenly seeing the letter you wrote in reply to my elder brother, radiant as spirits and gods, suddenly restores the old vision."
translations.idiomatic: Then I saw your answer to my brother—it shines like a work of the gods and brings that vision back in an instant."

sentences.zh: 時驃騎將軍王述少有名譽，與羲之齊名，而羲之甚輕之，由是情好不協。

translations.literal: At the time Cavalry-in-Attendant General Wang Shu had a minor reputation, with Xizhi equal name, but Xizhi greatly slighted him, whereby feelings and friendship not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Who Inspires Awe Wang Shu had enjoyed some fame and was ranked with Wang Xizhi, but Xizhi despised him, and the two never got along.

sentences.zh: 述先為會稽，以母喪居郡境，羲之代述，止一吊，遂不重詣。

translations.literal: Shu first was Kuaiji; because mother's mourning dwelt in commandery territory; Xizhi replaced Shu, only one condolence visit, then did not again visit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu had governed Kuaiji and, mourning his mother, stayed within the commandery when Wang Xizhi succeeded him. Xizhi paid a single condolence call and never returned.

sentences.zh: 述每聞角聲，謂羲之當候己，輒灑掃而待之。

translations.literal: Shu each time heard horn sound, thought Xizhi would await self, then sprinkled and swept and waited for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Shu heard a horn—thinking Xizhi might be coming—he swept his courtyard and waited.

sentences.zh: 如此者累年，而羲之竟不顧，述深以為恨。

translations.literal: Like this many years, yet Xizhi finally did not visit; Shu deeply took it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed, and Wang Xizhi never came; Wang Shu nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及述為揚州刺史，將就征，周行郡界，而不過羲之，臨發，一別而去。

translations.literal: When Shu became Inspector of Yang Province, about to take up summons, circuited the commandery border, yet did not pass Xizhi; on verge of departure, one farewell and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shu was appointed Inspector of Yang province, he toured the Kuaiji border on his way to take up the post but did not call on Xizhi; he paid one farewell visit only as he was leaving.

sentences.zh: 先是，羲之常謂賓友曰：「懷祖正當作尚書耳，投老可得僕射。

translations.literal: Before this, Xizhi often said to guests and friends, "Huai Zu ought only become Minister of Writing; casting old can obtain Vice Director."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Xizhi had told friends, "Huai Zu might rise to Minister of the Masters of Writing; in his old age he could make Vice Director."

sentences.zh: 更求會稽，便自邈然。

translations.literal: Further seeking Kuaiji, then is distant.
translations.idiomatic: As for Kuaiji again—that was beyond his reach."

sentences.zh: 」及述蒙顯授，羲之恥為之下，遣使詣朝廷，求分會稽為越州。

translations.literal: When Shu received eminent appointment, Xizhi ashamed to be below him, sent envoy to court, sought to divide Kuaiji into Yue Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shu won a lofty post, Wang Xizhi was humiliated at ranking beneath him and sent a messenger to court asking that Kuaiji be split off as a separate Yue province.

sentences.zh: 行人失辭，大為時賢所笑。

translations.literal: The envoy lost words, greatly by age's worthies was laughed at.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy bungled the plea and became a laughingstock among the eminent men of the day.

sentences.zh: 既而內懷愧歎，謂其諸子曰：「吾不減懷祖，而位遇懸邈，當由汝等不及坦之故邪！

translations.literal: Soon inwardly harboring shame and sigh, said to his various sons, "I am not inferior to Huai Zu, yet position and encounter hang distant—surely it is because you do not reach Tan's reason!"
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, he told his sons, "I am no less able than Huai Zu, yet our fortunes could not be more different—can it be because none of you measures up to his son Tan?"

sentences.zh: 」述後檢察會稽郡，辯其刑政，主者疲于簡對。

translations.literal: Shu later inspected Kuaiji commandery, debated its punishments and government; those in charge weary in document replies.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as inspector, Wang Shu audited Kuaiji's legal and administrative records; the clerks were worn out answering his queries.

sentences.zh: 羲之深恥之，遂稱病去郡，于父母墓前自誓曰：「維永和十一年三月癸卯朔，九日辛亥，小子羲之敢告二尊之靈。

translations.literal: Xizhi deeply shamed, then claimed illness and left commandery; before parents' tombs self-swore saying, "It is Yonghe eleventh year third month guimao new moon, ninth day xinhai, little son Xizhi dares announce to two venerables' spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi was mortified. He pleaded illness, resigned his post, and swore before his parents' graves: "On the ninth day of the third month of the eleventh year of Yonghe, xinhai day, your son Xizhi reverently addresses the spirits of both my parents."

sentences.zh: 羲之不天，夙遭閔凶，不蒙過庭之訓。

translations.literal: Xizhi not heaven, early met grievous misfortune, did not receive crossing-court's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven denied me parents early; I never received the lessons a son should have at his father's knee.

sentences.zh: 母兄鞠育，得漸庶幾，遂因人乏，蒙國寵榮。

translations.literal: Mother and elder brother raised and nurtured, was able gradually to near, then because of people's shortage, received state's favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: My mother and elder brother reared me until I amounted to something; when the state lacked men, I received undeserved honor.

sentences.zh: 進無忠孝之節，退違推賢之義，每仰詠老氏、周任之誡，常恐死亡無日，憂及宗祀，豈在微身而已！

translations.literal: Advancing without loyalty and filiality's integrity, retreating violates yielding to worthy's righteousness; often looking up chanting Laozi's, Zhou Ren's warnings, constantly fear death no day, worry reaching ancestral sacrifice—how only in slight self!
translations.idiomatic: In office I showed neither loyalty nor filial devotion; in retirement I failed the duty to yield to better men. I ponder Laozi's and Zhou Ren's warnings and fear my end may come any day, bringing ruin on the lineage—not on my person alone.

sentences.zh: 是用寤寐永歎，若墜深谷。

translations.literal: Therefore sleeping and waking long sigh, as if falling deep valley.
translations.idiomatic: I sigh awake and asleep as though I were tumbling into a chasm.

sentences.zh: 止足之分，定之於今。

translations.literal: Stopping and sufficing's portion, fix it in today.
translations.idiomatic: Today I fix the limit of what contentment requires.

sentences.zh: 謹以今月吉辰肆筵設席，稽顙歸誠，告誓先靈。

translations.literal: Respectfully with this month's auspicious morning spread mats set seats, knock forehead return sincerity, announce oath to former spirits.
translations.idiomatic: On this auspicious day I spread the ritual feast, bow my forehead to the ground, and in good faith declare my vow before you.

sentences.zh: 自今之後，敢渝此心，貪冒苟進，是有無尊之心而不子也。

translations.literal: From now after, dare betray this heart, greedy risk careless advance, this is having no respect heart and not being son.
translations.idiomatic: If from this day I break my word and grasp for rank, I shall be a son who no longer honors his parents.

sentences.zh: 子而不子，天地所不覆載，名教所不得容。

translations.literal: Son yet not son, what heaven and earth do not cover and bear, name-teaching cannot allow.
translations.idiomatic: Such a false son heaven and earth disown; the moral order cannot abide him.

sentences.zh: 信誓之誠，有如皦日！」

translations.literal: Sworn trust's sincerity, is like bright sun!"
translations.idiomatic: May this oath shine clear as the noon sun!"

sentences.zh: 羲之既去官，與東土人士盡山水之遊，弋釣為娛。

translations.literal: Xizhi having left office, with eastern lands' men of affairs exhausted mountains and waters' roaming, archery and fishing as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he roamed every scenic corner of the east with local friends, hunting and fishing for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 又與道士許邁共修服食，采藥石不遠千里，遍游東中諸郡，窮諸名山，泛滄海，歎曰：「我卒當以樂死。

translations.literal: Also with Daoist priest Xu Mai together cultivated ingesting medicines, gathering herbs and minerals not far a thousand li, everywhere roamed eastern middle various commanderies, exhausted various famous mountains, floated blue sea, sighed saying, "I finally ought to die of joy."
translations.idiomatic: With the Daoist Xu Mai he practiced dietetics and gathered herbs, traveling a thousand li without hesitation through the eastern commanderies and famous peaks, even putting out onto the sea, and sighed, "I shall end my days in bliss."

sentences.zh: 」謝安嘗謂羲之曰：「中年以來，傷於哀樂，與親友別，輒作數日惡。

translations.literal: Xie An once said to Xizhi, "Since middle years, wounded by sorrow and joy, parting from kin and friends, then become several days ill."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An once said to him, "Since middle age I am too easily moved; every parting from family or friends leaves me ill for days."

sentences.zh: 」羲之曰：「年在桑榆，自然至此。

translations.literal: Xizhi said, "Years at mulberry and elm, naturally arrive here."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi replied, "At the sunset of life it comes of itself."

sentences.zh: 頃正賴絲竹陶寫，恆恐兒輩覺，損其歡樂之趣。

translations.literal: Recently just relying on strings and bamboo to mold and write, constantly fear sons' generation noticing, diminishing their joy's interest.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I rely on music to ease my mood, yet I dread my children noticing—it would spoil the pleasure."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以其誓苦，亦不復征之。

translations.literal: The court because his oath was bitter, also did not again summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The court, respecting the sternness of his tomb-side vow, never called him back.

sentences.zh: 時劉惔為丹陽尹，許詢嘗就惔宿，床帷新麗，飲食豐甘。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Dan was Danyang Governor; Xu Xun once went to Dan to lodge, bed curtains new and lovely, drink and food abundant sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan was governor of Danyang. Xu Xun once stayed the night: fresh curtains, rich food.

sentences.zh: 詢曰：「若此保全，殊勝東山。

translations.literal: Xun said, "If thus preserved complete, surpasses East Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "If one could always live this safely, it would beat hiding on the Eastern Mountain."

sentences.zh: 」惔曰：「卿若知吉凶由人，吾安得保此。

translations.literal: Dan said, "If you knew fortune and misfortune follow men, how would I obtain preserve this."
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "If good and ill fortune were truly in our hands, I could not count on even this."

sentences.zh: 」羲之在坐，曰：「令巢許遇稷契，當無此言。

translations.literal: Xizhi being seated, said, "If made Chao Xu meet Ji Qi, ought have no such words."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi, who was present, said, "Had hermits like Chao Fu and Xu You met ministers like Ji and Qi, they would not speak so."

sentences.zh: 」二人並有愧色。

translations.literal: The two men together had ashamed looks.
translations.idiomatic: Both men colored with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 初，羲之既優遊無事，與吏部郎謝萬書曰：

translations.literal: At first, Xizhi having leisurely roamed without affairs, wrote to Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Xie Wan saying:
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Xizhi lived at leisure, he wrote to Xie Wan, the Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel:

sentences.zh: 古之辭世者或被髮陽狂，或汙身穢跡，可謂艱矣。

translations.literal: Ancient leavers of the age some disheveled hair feigned madness, some soiled body filthy traces—can be called hard.
translations.idiomatic: Men who quit the world in old times let their hair run wild or feigned madness, smeared themselves with filth—how hard their path was.

sentences.zh: 今僕坐而獲逸，遂其宿心，其為慶倖，豈非天賜！

translations.literal: Now your servant sitting obtains leisure, fulfills his long-held heart; its being celebratory luck—is it not heaven's gift!
translations.idiomatic: I sit at home and gain ease, fulfilling a lifelong wish—what luck; it feels like a gift from heaven.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥。

translations.literal: Violating heaven is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: To spurn heaven's favor would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 頃東游還，修植桑果，今盛敷榮，率諸子，抱弱孫，游觀其間，有一味之甘，割而分之，以娛目前。

translations.literal: Recently east roaming returned, planted mulberries and fruit; now luxuriantly spread glory, leading various sons, holding weak grandsons, roaming and viewing among them, having one flavor's sweetness, cut and divide it, to amuse before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Since my tour east I have tended mulberries and fruit; they flourish now. I lead my sons and carry little grandchildren through the orchards; if we find something sweet, we share it on the spot and take our joy from the moment.

sentences.zh: 雖植德無殊邈，猶欲教養子孫以敦厚退讓。

translations.literal: Although planting virtue not surpassingly distant, still wish to teach and nurture sons and grandsons with honest thick yielding yielding.
translations.idiomatic: I am no towering moral example, yet I hope to teach the children honesty, generosity, and modesty.

sentences.zh: 或以輕薄，庶令舉策數馬，仿佛萬石之風。

translations.literal: Perhaps with light thinness, hope to cause raising whip counting horses, roughly like ten thousand stone's wind.
translations.idiomatic: They may think me fussy, but I want them to learn to count the horses when they mount a carriage—something of the Wan-shi family's scrupulous style.

sentences.zh: 君謂此何如？

translations.literal: You say this how like?
translations.idiomatic: What do you think of that?

sentences.zh: 比當與安石東遊山海，並行田視地利，頤養閒暇。

translations.literal: Recently ought with An Shi east roam mountains and seas, together walk fields inspect land profit, nourish leisure idle.
translations.idiomatic: Next I shall tour the coast and hills eastward with Anshi, inspect the fields with him, and nurse my health in quiet.

sentences.zh: 衣食之餘，欲與親知時共歡宴，雖不能興言高詠，銜杯引滿，語田里所行，故以為撫掌之資，其為得意，可勝言邪！

translations.literal: Beyond clothes and food's remainder, wish with kin and friends sometimes together joyous feast; although cannot raise words high chant, hold cup draw full, speak fields' inside affairs, therefore take as clapping-palms' capital; its being satisfied intent—can it be fully said!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever we have more than we need for food and clothing, I want feasts with family and friends. We may not trade lofty verses, but we can drain our cups and talk of village life—that is enough to make us slap our knees with delight. Could words exhaust such contentment?

sentences.zh: 常依陸賈、班嗣、楊王孫之處世，甚欲希風數子，老夫志願盡於此也。

translations.literal: Constantly rely on Lu Jia, Ban Si, Yang Wangsun's dealing with the world; greatly wish to hope for wind of those several men; old man's aspiration ends in this.
translations.idiomatic: I model myself on Lu Jia, Ban Si, and Yang Wangsun; I long to catch something of their spirit. An old man's wishes go no further.

sentences.zh: 萬後為豫州都督，又遺萬書誡之曰：「以君邁往不屑之韻，而俯同群辟，誠難為意也。

translations.literal: Wan later became Yu Province Commander; again sent Wan letter warning saying, "With your lord's advancing past disdainful's tone, yet bowing same as group of petty officials, truly hard to make intention."
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Wan later became commander in Yuzhou, Wang Xizhi wrote again to caution him: "A man of your proud, fastidious temper must find it bitter to bend among common colleagues.

sentences.zh: 然所謂通識，正自當隨事行藏，乃為遠耳。

translations.literal: Yet so-called comprehensive insight, just ought follow affairs act or hide, then is far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet true breadth of mind means knowing when to step forward and when to hold back—that is what makes a man far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 願君每與士之下者同，則盡善矣。

translations.literal: Wish you lord each with gentlemen's below ones same, then exhaust good.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to meet your subordinates on their own level; that would be best.

sentences.zh: 食不二味，居不重席，此復何有，而古人以為美談。

translations.literal: Eating not two flavors, dwelling not double mat—this again what is there, yet ancients took as fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: To eat only one dish at a meal and use no double mat for sitting—what hardship is that? Yet the ancients praised it.

sentences.zh: 濟否所由。

translations.literal: Aid or not's whereby.
translations.idiomatic: Success and failure turn on such things.

sentences.zh: 實在積小以致高大，君其存之。

translations.literal: Truly lies in accumulating small to reach high great; you lord preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: Great character is built from small habits—bear that in mind."

sentences.zh: 」萬不能用，果敗。

translations.literal: Wan could not use it, indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan ignored the advice and met defeat as predicted.

sentences.zh: 年五十九卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At age fifty-nine died; posthumously awarded Golden Purple Splendid Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諸子遵父先旨，固讓不受。

translations.literal: The sons followed father's prior intent, firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, obeying his earlier wishes, firmly declined the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 子 凝之

translations.literal: Son: Ningzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Wang Ningzhi

sentences.zh: 有七子，知名者五人。

translations.literal: Had seven sons; of known name were five.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons, five of whom became well known.

sentences.zh: 玄之早卒。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi died early.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzhi died young.

sentences.zh: 次凝之，亦工草隸，仕歷江州刺史、左將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Next Ningzhi, also skilled in cursive and clerical; in office passed through Inspector of Jiang Province, General of the Left, Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Wang Ningzhi, also adept at cursive and clerical script, who served as Inspector of Jiang province, General of the Left, and internal administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 王氏世事張氏五斗米道，凝之彌篤。

translations.literal: The Wang clan for generations served the Zhang clan's Five Pecks of Rice Way; Ningzhi was more devout.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Wang family had followed the Zhangs' Way of the Five Pecks of Rice, and Ningzhi was the most fervent believer yet.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之攻會稽，僚佐請為之備。

translations.literal: When Sun En attacked Kuaiji, subordinate officials requested to make preparations for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En besieged Kuaiji, his staff urged him to prepare a defense.

sentences.zh: 凝之不從，方入靖室請禱，出語諸將佐曰：「吾已請大道，許鬼兵相助，賊自破矣。

translations.literal: Ningzhi did not follow; just entered quiet chamber to pray; coming out spoke to various generals and aides saying, "I have already asked the Great Way; it promised ghost soldiers to assist; the bandits will naturally be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi refused. He shut himself in the oratory to pray, then told his officers, "I have petitioned the Great Dao; spirit troops will aid us, and the rebels will destroy themselves."

sentences.zh: 」既不設備，遂為孫所害。

translations.literal: Since he did not set defenses, then was harmed by Sun.
translations.idiomatic: He made no military preparations and was killed by Sun En.

sentences.zh: 子 徽之

translations.literal: Son: Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Wang Huizhi

sentences.zh: 徽之字子猷。

translations.literal: Huizhi's courtesy name was Ziyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizhi, courtesy name Ziyou

sentences.zh: 性卓犖不羈，為大司馬桓溫參軍，蓬首散帶，不綜府事。

translations.literal: By nature outstanding and unrestrained; was Grand Marshal Huan Wen's army adviser, disheveled head loose belt, did not manage headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and unbent by nature. As army adviser to Grand Marshal Huan Wen he went about unkempt, sash dangling, and ignored administrative duty.

sentences.zh: 又為車騎桓沖騎兵參軍，沖問：「卿署何曹？

translations.literal: Also was Cavalry-in-Attendant Huan Chong's cavalry army adviser; Chong asked, "What bureau do you administer?"
translations.idiomatic: He later served as cavalry adviser to Huan Chong, the Cavalry-in-Attendant. Huan Chong asked, "Which section are you attached to?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「似是馬曹。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Seems like the horse bureau."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Something like the Horse Bureau, I suppose."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「管幾馬？

translations.literal: Again asked, "How many horses do you oversee?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many mounts are under your charge?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不知馬，何由知數！

translations.literal: Said, "Not knowing horses, how by that know the number!"
translations.idiomatic: "I know nothing of horses—how should I know the count?"

sentences.zh: 」又問：「馬比死多少？

translations.literal: Again asked, "Horses compared—how many died?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many of the horses have died lately?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「未知生，焉知死！

translations.literal: Said, "Not yet knowing life, how know death!"
translations.idiomatic: "We do not yet understand life—how could we speak of death?"

sentences.zh: 」嘗從沖行，值暴雨，徽之因下馬排入車中，謂曰：「公豈得獨擅一車！

translations.literal: Once followed Chong traveling, met violent rain; Huizhi therefore dismounted horse and pushed into the cart, saying, "Sir how can monopolize one cart!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding with Huan Chong in a cloudburst, he climbed from his horse into the carriage and said, "You cannot hog the whole vehicle to yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」沖嘗謂徽之曰：「卿在府日久，比當相料理。

translations.literal: Chong once said to Huizhi, "You have been in the headquarters long; recently ought to arrange for you."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong once told him, "You have been on staff a long time; it is time I found you real work."

sentences.zh: 」徽之初不酬答，直高視，以手版柱頰云：「西山朝來致有爽氣耳。」

translations.literal: Huizhi at first did not reply, only looked high, with hand tablet propping cheek saying, "Western hills this morning indeed have brisk air."
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi made no answer. He gazed into the distance, propped his cheek on his memorandum tablet, and said only, "The Western Hills have been wonderfully crisp all morning."

sentences.zh: 時吳中一士大夫家有好竹，欲觀之，便出坐輿造竹下，諷嘯良久。

translations.literal: At the time in Wu a scholar-official's household had fine bamboo; wishing to view it, then went out sat in sedan arrived under bamboo, intoned and whistled long.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman in Wu owned a superb bamboo grove. Huizhi rode straight there in an open chair, sat beneath the bamboos, and for a long while chanted and whistled.

sentences.zh: 主人灑掃請坐，徽之不顧。

translations.literal: The host sprinkled and swept inviting to sit; Huizhi did not look.
translations.idiomatic: The host swept a place and asked him in; Huizhi ignored him.

sentences.zh: 將出，主人乃閉門，徽之便以此賞之，盡歎而去。

translations.literal: About to leave, the host then closed the gate; Huizhi then by this appreciated him, fully sighed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, the host slammed the gate; Huizhi admired him for it, praised him wholeheartedly, and went away.

sentences.zh: 嘗寄居空宅中，便令種竹。

translations.literal: Once lodged in an empty house, then ordered bamboo planted.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging once in an empty house, he immediately had bamboo planted.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，徽之但嘯詠，指竹曰：「何可一日無此君邪！

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason; Huizhi only whistled and chanted, pointed at bamboo saying, "How can one day lack this lord!"
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he only whistled, pointed at the plants, and said, "How could I spend a single day without this gentleman?"

sentences.zh: 」嘗居山陰，夜雪初霽，月色清朗，四望皓然，獨酌酒詠左思《招隱詩》，忽憶戴逵。

translations.literal: Once dwelt in Shanyin; night snow first cleared, moonlight clear bright, four views white; alone poured wine and chanted Zuo Si's "Summoning the Recluse Poems"; suddenly remembered Dai Kui.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Shanyin he saw snow stop one night under a clear moon until the world gleamed white. He drank alone and recited Zuo Si's 《Summoning the Recluse》, and suddenly thought of Dai Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵時在剡，便夜乘小船詣之，經宿方至，造門不前而反。

translations.literal: Kui was then in Shan; then by night rode small boat went to him, after a night only arrived; reached gate did not advance but returned.
