translations.idiomatic: Dai was in Shan county, so Huizhi took a boat by night; it took until the next morning to arrive, yet he turned back without crossing the threshold.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，徽之曰：「本乘興而行，興盡而反，何必見安道邪！

translations.literal: People asked the reason; Huizhi said, "Originally rode impulse and went; impulse exhausted and returned—why must see An Dao!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked to explain, he said, "I went on a whim; when the mood was spent I came home—why did I need to see Andao?"

sentences.zh: 」雅性放誕，好聲色，嘗夜與弟獻之共讀《高士傳贊》，獻之賞井丹高潔，徽之曰：「未若長卿慢世也。

translations.literal: By nature unrestrained and wild, loved sound and color; once at night with younger brother Xianzhi together read 《Gaoshi Zhuan Zan》; Xianzhi praised Jing Dan's high purity; Huizhi said, "Not equal to Changqing's scorning the world."
translations.idiomatic: He was dissolute and fond of pleasure. One night he and his brother Xianzhi read the 《Eulogies to High-Minded Men》. Xianzhi admired Jing Dan's purity; Huizhi said, "He cannot match Sima Xiangru's contempt for the world."

sentences.zh: 」其傲達若此。

translations.literal: His proud openness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his proud unconventionality.

sentences.zh: 時人皆欽其才而穢其行。

translations.literal: People of the time all admired his talent yet deemed his conduct foul.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries honored his gifts but were revolted by his behavior.

sentences.zh: 後為黃門侍郎，棄官東歸，與獻之俱病篤，時有術人云：「人命應終，而有生人樂代者，則死者可生。

translations.literal: Later became Palace Attendant, abandoned office and east returned; with Xianzhi both critically ill; at the time a technician said, "Human fate ought to end, but if there is a living person gladly to substitute, then the dead can live."
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a Palace Attendant, then quit and went east. He and Xianzhi both lay near death when a occultist said, "When a man's span is up, if another willingly trades his years, the dying man may live."

sentences.zh: 」徽之謂曰：「吾才位不如弟，請以餘年代之。

translations.literal: Huizhi said to him, "My talent and position are not like younger brother's; please take my surplus years to substitute for him."
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi told him, "I am my brother's inferior in every way; take whatever years I have left and give them to him."

sentences.zh: 」術者曰：「代死者，以己年有餘，得以足亡者耳。

translations.literal: The technician said, "Substituting for the dead: with one's own years having surplus, able thereby to complete the deceased."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied, "Substitution works only when the donor's surplus of life can fill what the dead man lacked."

sentences.zh: 今君與弟算俱盡，何代也！

translations.literal: Now you lord and younger brother's reckoning both exhausted—what substitution!
translations.idiomatic: You and your brother have both reached your allotted end—there is nothing to exchange!"

sentences.zh: 」未幾，獻之卒，徽之奔喪不哭，直上靈床坐，取獻之琴彈之，久而不調，歎曰：「嗚呼子敬，人琴俱亡！

translations.literal: Before long, Xianzhi died; Huizhi rushed to mourning did not weep, straight ascended spirit couch sat, took Xianzhi's zither played it; long but not tuned; sighed saying, "Alas Zijing, person and zither both perished!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianzhi died. Huizhi hurried to the funeral but did not cry; he went straight to the bier, sat down, and took up Xianzhi's zither. The strings would not stay in tune. He cried, "O Zijing—the man is gone, and the instrument with him!"

sentences.zh: 」因頓絕。

translations.literal: Therefore collapsed and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off and fainted.

sentences.zh: 先有背疾，遂潰裂，月餘亦卒。

translations.literal: Earlier had back illness; then burst open; after a month more also died.
translations.idiomatic: An old abscess on his back broke open, and a little over a month later he too died.

sentences.zh: 子楨之。

translations.literal: Son: Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wang Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 徽之子 楨之

translations.literal: Huizhi's son: Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Wang Huizhi: Wang Zhenzhi

sentences.zh: 楨之字公幹，歷位侍中、大司馬長史。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi's courtesy name was Gonggan; passed through posts Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi, courtesy name Gonggan, rose to Palace Attendant and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 桓玄為太尉，朝臣畢集，問楨之：「我何如君亡叔？

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was Grand Commandant, court ministers all gathered; asked Zhenzhi, "How am I compared to your lord's deceased uncle?"
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan became Grand Commandant, the whole court assembled. He asked Zhenzhi, "How do I compare with your late uncle?"

sentences.zh: 」在坐咸為氣咽。

translations.literal: Those seated all were breath choked.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present held his breath.

sentences.zh: 楨之曰：「亡叔一時之標，公是千載之英。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi said, "Deceased uncle was one generation's standard; you lord are a thousand generations' hero."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi answered, "My uncle was the paragon of his age; you are a hero for the ages."

sentences.zh: 」一坐皆悅。

translations.literal: The whole seating all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company was pleased.

sentences.zh: 子 操之

translations.literal: Son: Caozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Wang Caozhi

sentences.zh: 操之字子重，曆侍中、尚書、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Caozhi's courtesy name was Zizhong; passed through Palace Attendant, Minister, Yuzhang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Caozhi, courtesy name Zizhong, served as Palace Attendant, Minister, and Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 子 獻之

translations.literal: Son: Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Wang Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 獻之字子敬。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's courtesy name was Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi, courtesy name Zijing

sentences.zh: 少有盛名，而高邁不羈，雖閒居終日，容止不怠，風流為一時之冠。

translations.literal: In youth had great fame, yet lofty and unrestrained; although idle dwelling whole day, bearing and demeanor not slack; elegance was one generation's crown.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated from boyhood, he was proud and free-spirited. Even at leisure all day he never let his bearing slip, and for grace he had no peer in his time.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，嘗觀門生樗蒱，曰：「南風不競。

translations.literal: Aged several years, once watched disciples chupu, said, "South wind not competing."
translations.idiomatic: Watching his father's disciples play chupu while still a child, he remarked, "The southern player is losing ground."

sentences.zh: 」門生曰：「此郎亦管中窺豹，時見一斑。

translations.literal: The disciple said, "This lad also peeks at leopard through a tube, sometimes sees one spot."
translations.idiomatic: A disciple said, "The boy is peering at a leopard through a bamboo tube—he catches only a single spot."

sentences.zh: 」獻之怒曰：「遠慚荀奉倩，近愧劉真長。

translations.literal: Xianzhi angrily said, "Far ashamed before Xun Fengqian, near ashamed before Liu Zhenchang."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi flared: "Compared with Xun Can in the past or Liu Tan among our own circle, I am ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」遂拂衣而去。

translations.literal: Then brushed robe and left.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his sleeves aside and walked out.

sentences.zh: 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安，二兄多言俗事，獻之寒溫而已。

translations.literal: Once with elder brothers Huizhi, Caozhi together visited Xie An; two elder brothers much spoke vulgar affairs; Xianzhi only cold-warm.
translations.idiomatic: Once he went with Huizhi and Caozhi to visit Xie An. The elder brothers talked of trivial matters; Xianzhi offered only polite greetings.

sentences.zh: 既出，客問安王氏兄弟優劣，安曰：「小者佳。

translations.literal: After leaving, guests asked An Wang clan brothers' good and bad; An said, "The small one is best."
translations.idiomatic: After they left, a guest asked which brother was superior. Xie An said, "The youngest."

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，安曰：「吉人之辭寡，以其少言，故知之。

translations.literal: Guest asked the reason; An said, "A good man's words are few; because of his little speech, therefore know it."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Good men say little; his silence told me."

sentences.zh: 」嘗與徽之共在一室，忽然火發，徽之遽走，不遑取履。

translations.literal: Once with Huizhi together in one room; suddenly fire broke out; Huizhi hurriedly ran, no time to take shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and Huizhi were in the same room when fire broke out. Huizhi bolted without stopping for his shoes.

sentences.zh: 獻之神色恬然，徐呼左右扶出。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's spirit color was calm; slowly called attendants to help him out.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi stayed perfectly calm and told his servants to help him out at leisure.

sentences.zh: 夜臥齋中而有偷人入其室，盜物都盡。

translations.literal: Night lying in studio yet there was a thief entering his room; stolen goods all gone.
translations.idiomatic: One night thieves entered his study while he slept and stripped the room bare.

sentences.zh: 獻之徐曰：「偷兒，氈青我家舊物，可特置之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi slowly said, "Thief lads, the felt green is our house's old object; can specially set it aside."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said calmly, "Thieves—that dark felt mat is a family heirloom; kindly leave it."

sentences.zh: 」群偷驚走。

translations.literal: The group of thieves startled and ran.
translations.idiomatic: The robbers fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，善丹青。

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive and clerical; good at cinnabar-green.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical script and was a fine painter.

sentences.zh: 七八歲時學書，羲之密從後掣其筆不得，歎曰：「此兒後當復有大名。

translations.literal: At seven or eight years studying writing, Xizhi secretly from behind pulled his brush but could not obtain; sighed saying, "This child later will again have great name."
translations.idiomatic: At seven or eight, while practicing calligraphy, his father tried to tug the brush from behind and could not. Wang Xizhi sighed, "This boy will make a great name for himself."

sentences.zh: 」嘗書壁為方丈大字，羲之甚以為能，觀者數百人。

translations.literal: Once wrote on wall as one zhang square large characters; Xizhi greatly thought him capable; viewers several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: He once brushed characters a full square foot high on a wall. His father was deeply impressed, and hundreds came to watch.

sentences.zh: 桓溫嘗使書扇，筆誤落，因畫作烏駁牸牛，甚妙。

translations.literal: Huan Wen once had him write on a fan; brush mistakenly dropped; therefore painted as dappled black cow, very subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen once asked him to write on a fan. The brush slipped, so he turned the blot into a dappled black cow—brilliantly done.

sentences.zh: 起家州主簿、秘書郎，轉丞，以選尚新安公主。

translations.literal: Rose from family as provincial chief clerk, Palace Secretary, transferred to aide; by selection married Princess of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a provincial chief clerk and Gentleman of the Palace Library, became an aide, and by imperial selection married the Princess of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 嘗經吳郡，聞顧辟彊有名園。

translations.literal: Once passed through Wu commandery, heard Gu Piqiang had a famous garden.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wu commandery, he heard that Gu Piqiang owned a celebrated garden.

sentences.zh: 先不相識，乘平肩輿徑入。

translations.literal: Previously not knowing each other, rode level-shoulder sedan straight in.
translations.idiomatic: They were strangers, yet Xianzhi rode a plain sedan chair straight through the gate.

sentences.zh: 時辟彊方集賓友，而獻之遊歷既畢，傍若無人。

translations.literal: At the time Piqiang was just gathering guests and friends, yet Xianzhi's touring finished, beside as if no people.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was entertaining guests. Xianzhi toured the grounds as if no one else were there.

sentences.zh: 辟彊勃然數之曰：「傲主人，非禮也。

translations.literal: Piqiang suddenly rebuked him saying, "Arrogant to the host is not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Gu exploded: "To insult your host breaks every rule of courtesy.

sentences.zh: 以貴驕士，非道也。

translations.literal: By nobility to lord it over gentlemen is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To throw your rank at a scholar is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 失是二者，不足齒之傖耳。

translations.literal: Losing these two is not worth teeth's vulgar fellow.
translations.idiomatic: A man who fails on both counts is beneath contempt."

sentences.zh: 」便驅出門。

translations.literal: Then drove out the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He had him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 獻之傲如也，不以屑意。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was proud as before, did not regard it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi remained loftily unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 謝安甚欽愛之，請為長史。

translations.literal: Xie An greatly admired and loved him, invited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An admired him deeply and appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 安進號衛將軍，復為長史。

translations.literal: An advanced title General Who Guards the Army, again was chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie An was promoted to General Who Guards the Army, Xianzhi again served as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 太元中，新起太極殿，安欲使獻之題榜，以為萬代寶，而難言之，試謂曰：「魏時陵雲殿榜未題，而匠者誤釘之，不可下，乃使韋仲將懸橙書之。

translations.literal: In Taiyuan era, newly built Supreme Ultimate Hall; An wished to make Xianzhi inscribe the plaque, thinking it a treasure for ten thousand generations, yet hard to speak; tried saying, "Wei times Lingyun Hall plaque not yet inscribed, yet craftsmen mistakenly nailed it, could not take down, then sent Wei Zhongjiang suspended orange to write it."
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan era the new Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was raised. Xie An wanted Xianzhi to write the hall plaque—a treasure for all time—but hesitated to ask outright. He began obliquely: "Under Wei, the Lingyun Hall plaque was nailed up before anyone had brushed the characters. When the board could not be removed, they had Wei Dan hoisted on a scaffold to write it."

sentences.zh: 比訖，須鬢盡白，裁餘氣息。

translations.literal: When finished, beard and sideburns all white, barely remaining breath.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, his beard had gone white and he could barely breathe.

sentences.zh: 還語子弟，宜絕此法。

translations.literal: Returning told sons and younger brothers, ought to cut off this method.
translations.idiomatic: He told his sons never to attempt such a thing again.

sentences.zh: 」獻之揣知其旨，正色曰：「仲將，魏之大臣，甯有此事！

translations.literal: Xianzhi guessed and knew its purport, with stern color said, "Zhong Jiang, Wei's great minister—how could there be this affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi saw the point and answered gravely, "Zhongjiang was a high minister of Wei—such a story cannot be true."

sentences.zh: 使其若此，有以知魏德之不長。

translations.literal: If it were thus, there is means to know Wei's virtue was not long.
translations.idiomatic: If it were true, it would only show how shallow Wei virtue ran."

sentences.zh: 」安遂不之逼。

translations.literal: An then did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 安又問曰：「君書何如君家尊？

translations.literal: An again asked saying, "Your lord's writing how compared to your lord's family's venerable?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie An asked again, "How does your calligraphy compare with your father's?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「故當不同。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Solidly ought to differ."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "They are simply different."

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「外論不爾。

translations.literal: An said, "Outside opinion not so."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An said, "Outsiders do not say so."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「人那得知！

translations.literal: Replied saying, "People how can know!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "What do outsiders know of it?"

sentences.zh: 」尋除建威將軍、吳興太守，徵拜中書令。

translations.literal: Soon removed as General Who Establishes Might, Wuxing Administrator; summoned appointed Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was named General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Wuxing, then summoned as Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，獻之遇疾，家人為上章，道家法應首過，問其有何得失。

translations.literal: Before long, Xianzhi met illness; family members for him submitted petition; Daoist law should confess faults, asked what faults and gains he had.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xianzhi fell ill. His family filed a Daoist petition of confession and asked him what sins he needed to acknowledge.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不覺餘事，惟憶與郗家離婚。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Not aware of other matters; only remember divorcing the Xi family."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I recall nothing else but divorcing my wife from the Xi clan."

sentences.zh: 」獻之前妻，郗曇女也。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's former wife was Xi Tan's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's first wife had been a daughter of Xi Tan.

sentences.zh: 俄而卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 安僖皇后立，以後父追贈侍中、特進、光祿大夫、太宰，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: Empress Anxi established; because empress's father posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Governor, posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Anxi was installed, her father Wang Xianzhi was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Governor with the posthumous title "Xian."

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子靜之嗣，位至義興太守。

translations.literal: Without son, with elder brother's son Jingzhi as heir; position reached Yixing Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his nephew Wang Jingzhi became his heir and rose to Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 時議者以為羲之草隸，江左中朝莫有及者，獻之骨力遠不及父，而頗有媚趣。

translations.literal: Contemporary debaters thought Xizhi's cursive and clerical, Jiangzuo and central court none reached him; Xianzhi's bone force far did not reach father, yet had quite charming interest.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that in cursive and clerical script Wang Xizhi had no rival south of the Yangzi or at the old capital; Xianzhi's stroke lacked his father's vigor but showed a seductive charm of its own.

sentences.zh: 桓玄雅愛其父子書，各為一帙，置左右以玩之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan elegantly loved father and son's writing, each made one bundle, placed left and right to play with.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan treasured the brush of father and son; he kept a separate album of each at hand for his delight.

sentences.zh: 始羲之所與共游者許邁。

translations.literal: At first Xizhi's with whom together roamed was Xu Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Among those with whom Wang Xizhi first roamed the hills was Xu Mai.

sentences.zh: 附 許邁

translations.literal: Attached: Xu Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Xu Mai

sentences.zh: 許邁，字叔玄，一名映，丹陽句容人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mai, courtesy name Shuxuan, another name Ying, was a man of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mai, whose courtesy name was Shuxuan and who was also known as Ying, came from Jurong in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世士族，而邁少恬靜，不慕仕進。

translations.literal: Family generations scholar clan, yet Mai in youth was quiet and calm, did not admire office advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Though his clan belonged to the gentry, Mai was quiet and retiring from youth and cared nothing for an official career.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，嘗造郭璞，璞為之筮，遇《泰》之《大畜》，其上六爻發。

translations.literal: Before capping, once visited Guo Pu; Pu for him divined, met Tai's Da Chu, its top sixth line moved.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping year he visited Guo Pu, who cast the yarrow for him and obtained the hexagram Tai changing to Da Chu, with the top line moving.

sentences.zh: 璞謂曰：「君元吉自天，宜學升遐之道。

translations.literal: Pu said to him, "You lord's great auspiciousness comes from heaven; ought to study ascending-far's Way."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu told him, "Supreme good fortune reaches you from on high; you should pursue the path of transcendence."

sentences.zh: 」時南海太守鮑靚隱跡潛遁，人莫之知。

translations.literal: At the time Nanhai Administrator Bao Jing hid traces and submerged away; people none knew him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bao Jing, the Administrator of Nanhai, had vanished into reclusion and was unknown to the world.

sentences.zh: 邁乃往候之，探其至要。

translations.literal: Mai then went to visit him, explored his utmost essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Mai sought him out and drew from him the heart of the teaching.

sentences.zh: 父母尚存，未忍違親。

translations.literal: Father and mother still existed; not yet bear to violate kin.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were still alive, and he could not bear to leave them.

sentences.zh: 謂余杭懸霤山近延陵之茅山，是洞庭西門，潛通五嶽，陳安世、茅季偉常所遊處，於是立精舍於懸霤，而往來茅嶺之洞室，放絕世務，以尋仙館，朔望時節還家定省而已。

translations.literal: He said Yuhang's Xuansliu Mountain neared Yanling's Mao Mountain, was Dongting's west gate, secretly connected to Five Peaks; Chen Anshi, Mao Jiwei's constant roaming place; therefore established a retreat on Xuansliu, and went back and forth to Mao Ridge's cave chambers, releasing and cutting worldly affairs, to seek immortal lodges; new and full moon seasons returned home to visit parents only.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Mount Xuansliu in Yuhang, near Mount Mao by Yanling, was the western portal of Dongting and linked invisibly to the Five Marchmounts—the ground where Chen Anshi and Mao Jiwei had roamed. There he built a hermitage and moved between the caves on Mao Ridge, turning his back on the world to seek the immortals' abodes, coming home only at the new and full moons to greet his parents.

sentences.zh: 父母既終，乃遣婦孫氏還家，遂攜其同志遍游名山焉。

translations.literal: Parents having ended, then sent wife Lady Sun back home, then carried his like-minded to roam famous mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he sent his wife, née Sun, back to her family and set out with fellow seekers to wander every famous peak.

sentences.zh: 初采藥於桐廬縣之桓山，餌術涉三年，時欲斷穀。

translations.literal: At first gathered herbs at Tonglu county's Huan Mountain, ingested atractylodes spanning three years, at times wished to cut grain.
translations.idiomatic: He first gathered drugs on Mount Huan in Tonglu county, fed on atractylodes for three years, and tried to abstain from grain.

sentences.zh: 以此山近人，不得專一，四面籓之，好道之徒欲相見者，登樓與語，以此為樂。

translations.literal: Because this mountain neared people, could not obtain single focus; fenced it on four sides; those who loved the Way wishing to meet, ascended tower and spoke with them, taking this as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mountain lay too close to settlers for undisturbed practice, he fenced it on every side. Seekers who wished to see him were made to climb a tower and speak from there—an arrangement he found amusing.

sentences.zh: 常服氣，一氣千餘息。

translations.literal: Constantly ingested breath; one breath over a thousand exhalations.
translations.idiomatic: In breath meditation he would hold a single cycle through more than a thousand counts.

sentences.zh: 永和二年，移入臨安西山，登岩茹芝，眇爾自得，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Yonghe second year, moved into Lin'an western mountains, climbed crags ate fungus, subtly self-content, had will to end there.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghe he moved to the western hills of Lin'an, climbed the cliffs, fed on mushroom elixirs, and found a quiet joy; he resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 乃改名玄，字遠遊。

translations.literal: Then changed name to Xuan, courtesy name Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the name Xuan and the courtesy name Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 與婦書告別，又著詩十二首，論神仙之事焉。

translations.literal: To wife wrote farewell; also composed twelve poems, discussing immortal matters.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife a letter of farewell and wrote twelve poems on the subject of transcendents.

sentences.zh: 羲之造之，未嘗不彌日忘歸，相與為世外之交。

translations.literal: Xizhi visited him, never not filling the day forgetting return; with each other became beyond-the-world's friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Xizhi visited, the two would talk the whole day through; they were friends outside the common world.

sentences.zh: 玄遺羲之書云：「自山陰南至臨安，多有金堂玉室，仙人芝草，左元放之徒，漢末諸得道者皆在焉。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Xizhi a letter saying, "From Shanyin south to Lin'an, many have golden halls jade chambers, immortal fungus grass; Zuo Yuanfang's sort, Han end various who obtained the Way all are there."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote to Wang Xizhi: "South from Shanyin to Lin'an lie halls of gold and chambers of jade, spirit herbs, and the company of Zuo Ci—all who attained the Way at the end of the Han are there."

sentences.zh: 」羲之自為之傳，述靈異之跡甚多，不可詳記。

translations.literal: Xizhi himself for him made a biography, narrating numinous wonders' traces very many, cannot detail record.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi himself composed his biography, recording marvels too numerous to set down in full.

sentences.zh: 玄自後莫測所終，好道者皆謂之羽化矣。

translations.literal: Xuan from afterward none could fathom where he ended; those who loved the Way all called it feather-transformation.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one knew his fate; adepts said he had ascended in feathered form.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：書契之興，肇乎中古，繩文鳥跡，不足可觀。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Writing's rise began in middle antiquity; knotted-pattern bird-tracks, not worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment runs: Writing arose in high antiquity from knotted cords and bird-track glyphs—scarcely worth our notice.

sentences.zh: 末代去朴歸華，舒箋點翰，爭相跨尚，競其工拙。

translations.literal: Final age left plain returned to splendor; spread paper dot brush; striving to leap and esteem, competing their skill and clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages turned from plainness to ornament: paper unrolled, brushes dipped, each school vying to outdo the rest in skill or clumsiness.

sentences.zh: 伯英臨池之妙，無復餘蹤；

translations.literal: Bo Ying by the pond's subtlety, no again remaining traces;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi's miracle at the pond survives only in legend;

sentences.zh: 師宜懸帳之奇，罕有遺跡。

translations.literal: Shi Yi suspended curtain's marvel, rarely has remaining traces.
translations.idiomatic: and Shi Yiguan's feat with the hanging curtain has left almost no authentic trace.

sentences.zh: 逮乎鐘王以降，略可言焉。

translations.literal: Down to Zhong and Wang and below, briefly can be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Only from Zhong Yao and the Wangs onward can one speak with confidence.

sentences.zh: 鐘雖擅美一時，亦為回絕，論其盡善，或有所疑。

translations.literal: Zhong although monopolized beauty one generation, also was surpassing unique; discussing his exhaustive good, perhaps has doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao dominated his age, head and shoulders above rivals, yet whether he achieved perfect excellence remains debatable.

sentences.zh: 至於布纖濃，分疏密，霞舒雲卷，無所間然。

translations.literal: As for arranging fine and thick, dividing sparse and dense, rosy clouds spread clouds roll—nothing obstructs thus.
translations.idiomatic: In laying fine and bold strokes, spacing tight and open lines, he moves like mist parting and clouds curling—without a false step.

sentences.zh: 但其體則古而不今，字則長而逾制，語其大量，以此為瑕。

translations.literal: But his style then is ancient yet not modern; characters then long yet exceed regulation; speaking his great measure, by this as flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his manner is archaic rather than contemporary, and his characters overlong for the rule—in the round, those are blemishes.

sentences.zh: 獻之雖有父風，殊非新巧。

translations.literal: Xianzhi although has father's wind, utterly not new cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi echoes his father but brings little fresh ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 觀其字勢疏瘦，如隆冬之枯樹；

translations.literal: Observe his character momentum sparse thin, like deep winter's withered tree;
translations.idiomatic: The structure of his hand is gaunt as a winter tree stripped bare;

sentences.zh: 覽其筆蹤拘束，若嚴家之餓隸。

translations.literal: View his brush traces constrained, like a strict family's starving bondservant.
translations.idiomatic: his strokes are cramped like a famished bondsman in a harsh master's house.

sentences.zh: 其枯樹也，雖槎枿而無屈伸；

translations.literal: That withered tree, although stump-sprout yet without bending stretching;
translations.idiomatic: That winter tree is a dead snag without spring or flex;

sentences.zh: 其餓隸也，則羈羸而不放縱。

translations.literal: That starving bondservant, then tethered lean yet not unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: that bondsman is haltered, wasted, never free to move.

sentences.zh: 兼斯二者，故翰墨之病歙！

translations.literal: Combining these two, therefore brush-ink's sickness sucks!
translations.idiomatic: Both faults together make a sickness in the brush!

sentences.zh: 子雲近出，擅名江表，然僅得成書，無丈夫之氣，行行若縈春蚓，字字如綰秋蛇；

translations.literal: Ziyun recently emerged, monopolized name south of the river, yet only obtained completed writing, without great man's qi; line after line as if winding spring earthworms; character after character as if coiling autumn snakes;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziyun rose later and ruled the calligraphy of the south, yet he merely forms legible script without a man's vigor: each line wriggles like spring worms; each character knots like autumn snakes;

sentences.zh: 臥王濛於紙中，坐徐偃於筆下；

translations.literal: Lay Wang Meng in the paper; seat Xu Yan under the brush;
translations.idiomatic: it is Wang Meng stretched ill on the page, Xu Yan the hunchback crouching under the brush;

sentences.zh: 雖禿千兔之翰，聚無一毫之筋，窮萬谷之皮，斂無半分之骨；

translations.literal: Although pluck a thousand rabbits' brushes, gather not one hair's sinew; exhaust ten thousand valleys' bark, collect not half a fraction's bone;
translations.idiomatic: though you wear out a forest of rabbit brushes, not a fiber of strength appears; though you stack hides from every valley, not half a splinter of bone remains;

sentences.zh: 以茲播美，非其濫名邪！

translations.literal: By this spread beauty—is it not his excessive name!
translations.idiomatic: to praise such work is to inflate a hollow reputation!

sentences.zh: 此數子者，皆譽過其實。

translations.literal: These several men, all fame exceeds their reality.
translations.idiomatic: These men are all more famous than they deserve.

sentences.zh: 所以詳察古今，研精篆素，盡善盡美，其惟王逸少乎！

translations.literal: Therefore carefully examine ancient and modern, grind fine seal on plain—exhaust good exhaust beauty—who but Wang Yishao!
translations.idiomatic: Survey past and present, study every seal-script master on silk, and who attains full goodness and full beauty if not Wang Yishao?

sentences.zh: 觀其點曳之工，裁成之妙，煙霏露結，狀若斷而還連；

translations.literal: Observe his dot-drag's craft, cut-complete's subtlety: mist float dew knot, appearance as if broken yet still linked;
translations.idiomatic: See the mastery of his dots and sweeps, the perfection of his composition: mist and dew congeal in forms that seem broken yet still flow together;

sentences.zh: 鳳翥龍蟠，勢如斜而反直。

translations.literal: Phoenix soar dragon coil, momentum as if slanting yet contrary straight.
translations.idiomatic: phoenix poised, dragon coiled—energy that looks slanted yet stands upright.

sentences.zh: 玩之不覺為倦，覽之莫識其端，心慕手追，此人而已。

translations.literal: Playing with it not aware of weariness; viewing it none knows its end; heart admires hand pursues—this man alone.
translations.idiomatic: One could study it without tiring, yet never trace its limit; heart envies and hand follows—only this man.

sentences.zh: 其餘區區之類，何足論哉！

translations.literal: The rest petty sorts—how worth discussing!
translations.idiomatic: The rest are small fry—not worth a word!
